tinue or curtail a motor-vehicle pool or 
system when he determines that it is 
not the most economical method of ren­
dering required motor-vehicle service; 
but he shall give at least sixty days no­
tice of such intention to executive agen­
cies affected and to the Director before 
taking such action.
(c) Executive agencies affected by a 
pool or system for which the Adminis­
trator is responsible (including inter­
agency pools or systems operated by an­
other executive agency designated by the 
Administrator) may bring problems of 
service and cost to the attention of the. 
Administrator, who shall assure that 
such problems receive proper attention.
(d) Executive agencies  receiving 
motor-vehicle services from an inter­
agency motor-vehicle pool or system 
under these regulations may request dis­
continuance or curtailment of their par­
ticipation in such pool or system after 
at least one year of participation or in 
the event that the need for the services 
from the pool or system ceases. Such 
requests shall be submitted to the Ad­
ministrator with pertinent factual justi­
fication.
(e) If the Administrator does not 
agree with such request and is unable to 
make arrangements which are mutually 
acceptable to him and to the head of the 
executive agency concerned, the agency’ s 
request for discontinuance or modifica­
tion and the Administrator’ s reasons for 
not agreeing with the request shall be 
forwarded to the Director who shall be 
responsible for making a final and bind­
ing decision.
(f) When a pool or system is discon­
tinued or curtailed, such transfers of 
vehicles and related equipment and sup­
plies, personnel, records, facilities, and 
funds as may be appropriate will be 
made, subject to the approval of the 
Director.
S ec. 9. Motor vehicles exempted from  
inclusion in interagency motor-vehicle  
pools. The following-described classes 
of motor vehicles shall be exempt from 
inclusion in\ interagency motor-vehicle 
pools or systems:
(1) Motor vehicles designed or used 
for military field training, combat, or 
tactical purposes, or used principally 
within the confines of a regularly estab­
lished military post, camp, or depot.
(2) Any motor vehicle regularly used 
by an agency in the performance of in­
vestigative, law enforcement, or intelli­
gence duties if the head of such agency 
determines that exclusive control of such 
vehicle is essential to the effective per­
formance of such duties: Provided, that 
vehicles regularly used for common ad­
ministrative purposes not directly con­
nected with the performance of law 
enforcement, investigative, or intelli­
gence duties shall not because of such 
use be exempted from such inclusion.
(3) Any motor vehicle the conspicu­
ous identification of which as a Govern­
ment vehicle would interfere with the 
purpose for which it is acquired and 
used.
(4) Unless inclusion is mutually agreed 
upon by the Administrator and the head 
of the agency concerned:
(i) Motor vehicles for the use of the 
heads of the executive agencies, ambas­
sadors, ministers, chargé d’ affaires, and 
other principal diplomatic and consular 
officials.
(ii) Motor vehicles regularly and prin­
cipally used for the transportation of 
diplomats and representatives of foreign 
countries or by officers of the Depart­
ment of State for the conduct of official 
business with representatives of foreign 
countries.
(iii) Motor vehicles regularly used for 
the distribution and transportation of 
mails.
(5) Motor vehicles which, because of 
their design or the special purposes for 
which they are used, or for other reasons, 
cannot advantageously be incorporated 
in an interagency motor-vehicle pool or 
system if the exemption thereof has been 
mutually agreed upon by the Adminis­
trator and the head of the executive 
agency concerned.
(6) Motor vehicles exempted by an 
agency which ljas authority to make such 
an exemption under the provisions of the 
Act.
S ec. 10. Optional use arrangements.  
Nothing in these regulations shall be 
construed as precluding the establish­
ment or operation of interagency motor- 
vehicle pools or systems on the basis of 
optional use by executive or other Fed­
eral agencies.
S ec. 11. Supplementary regulations.  
The Administrator shall, after consulta­
tion with the executive agencies con­
cerned and with due regard to their 
program activities, issue such supple­
mentary regulations of general applica­
bility to the executive agencies concerned 
as are necessary for the effective and eco­
nomical operation of pools or systems 
under the Act.

Section 9 lists classes of motor vehicles exempt from interagency pools: military field-training, combat and tactical vehicles; investigative, law-enforcement and intelligence vehicles that the agency head determines need exclusive control; vehicles whose conspicuous identification as Government vehicles would interfere with their purpose; vehicles for agency heads and principal diplomatic and consular officials, diplomatic transport vehicles and mail vehicles unless inclusion is mutually agreed; special-purpose vehicles whose exemption is mutually agreed; and vehicles exempted by an agency with authority under the Act. The exemptions are a continuing list. It has no own-terms end, and no held instrument ends or amends it.

By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Federal Property and Adminis­
trative Services Act of 1949, as amended 
(hereinafter referred to as the Act), 
particularly by sections 107, 205 (a) and 
211 (c) thereof, 63 Stat. 382, 389, 64 Stat. 
580, and 68 Stat. 1126, and by^section 202 
of the Budget and Accounting Proce­
dures Act of 1950 (64 Stat. 838; 31U. S. C. 
581c), and as President of the United 
States, I hereby prescribe the following 
regulations: t
S ection  1. Purpose and general policy.
(a) The purpose of these regulations is 
to establish policies and procedures un­
der which interagency motor-vehicle 
pools or systems may be established, op­
erated, curtailed, or discontinued.
(b) The Administrator of General 
Services (hereinafter referred to as the 
Administrator) shall establish and pro­
vide for the operation of interagency 
motor-vehicle pools and systems for the 
purpose of providing more efficient or 
economical transportation of Govern­
ment personnel and property within 
specific areas by motor vehicles or local 
transit systems. Pools or systems based 
in whole or in part upon use of privately- 
owned vehicles and facilities shall be 
preferred to Government ownership of 
vehicles and facilities to the extent that 
it is feasible to provide required motor- 
vehicle services of satisfactory quality 
and cost from commercial or other pri­
vate sources.
Sec. 2. Conduct of studies to deter­
mine advisability  o f establishing  
motor-vehicle pools or systems, (a) The 
Administrator shall select areas in which 
studies are to be conducted to determine 
the advisability of establishing motor- 
vehicle pools or systems. Before initiat­
ing any such study, he shall give at least 
thirty days notice to the head of each 
executive agency (as defined in section 
3 (a) of the Act). The notice shall in­
clude a statement of the approximate 
geographic area to be studied and the 
date on which the study will begin.
(b) The head of each executive agency 
receiving notice that such a study is to
be made shall provide information which 
is required or pertinent. He shall also 
designate one or more officials in the 
field with whom members of a staff as­
signed by the General Services Admin­
istration may consult. Such designated 
officials shall provide such assigned staff 
with needed information and assistance, 
including reasonable opportunities to 
observe motor-vehicle operations and 
facilities and to examine pertinent cost 
and other records.
Sec.  3. Determination to establish an  
interagency motor-vehicle pool or sys­
tem. (a) If the Administrator deter­
mines, with due regard to the program 
activities of the agencies concerned, and 
on the basis of a study made in accord­
ance with section 2 hereof, that an inter­
agency motor-vehicle pool or system 
should be established, he shall be respon­
sible for preparing a formal determina­
tion to that effect. Such determination 
shall include:(1) A description of the proposed op­
eration, including a statement of the 
types of service and of the geographic 
area, and the agencies or parts of agen­
cies to be served.(2) The name of the executive agency 
designated to be responsible for operat­
ing the pool or system, and the reasons 
for such designation.
(3) A statement indicating the motor 
vehicles and related equipment and sup­
plies to be transferred and the amount 
of reimbursement, if any, to be made 
therefor.
(b) Each determination shall be ac­
companied by an analytical justification 
which shall include a comparison of 
estimated costs of the present and pro­
posed methods of operation and a show­
ing of the estimated savings to be real­
ized through the establishment of the 
proposed pool or system. The justifica­
tion shall also describe the alternatives 
considered in making the determination, 
and shall include a statement concern­
ing the availability of privately-owned 
facilities and equipment, and the feasi­
bility and estimated cost (immediate and 
long-term) of using such facilities and 
equipment.
(c) The Administrator shall send a 
copy of each determination to each exec­
utive agency affected and to the Director

rector shall make such decisions, within 
seventy-five days after he receives the 
appeal or as soon thereafter as prac­
ticable, on the basis of information con­
tained in the Administrator’ s determi­
nation, the executive agencies’  appeals 
therefrom, and any supplementary data 
submitted by the Administrator and the 
contesting agencies. The Director shall 
send copies of decisions to the Adminis­
trator and to the heads of other execu­
tive agencies concerned.
(c) The Director’ s decision upon each 
such appeal, if it holds that the deter­
mination shall apply in whole or in part 
to the appealing agency, shall state the 
extent to which the determination ap­
plies and the effective date of its appli­
cation. To the extent that the Director’ s 
decision on an appeal does not uphold 
the Administrator’ s determination, such 
determination shall be of no force and 
effect.
S ec. 7. Compliance with determina­
tions and decisions on appeals, (a) When 
a determination or a decision on an ap­
peal made in accordance with these 
regulations has become effective, each 
executive agency affected shall comply 
therewith.(b) The Director shall take such ac­
tions as he deems appropriate to assist 
in securing compliance with determina­
tions which have become effective. In 
the exercise of his authority to establish 
reserves in apportioning appropriations 
and funds, the Director shall take ac­
count of such savings as accrue from 
the establishment of interagency motor- 
vehicle pools and systems.
(c) The executive agency which op­
erates any pool or system established 
hereunder shall maintain accurate rec­
ords of the cost of establishment, main­
tenance, and operation of any inter­
agency motor-vehicle pool or system 
established pursuant to these regula­
tions.
(d) The Administrator shall be re­
sponsible for maintaining adequate re­
views and controls of the economy and
efficiency of all pools or systems estab­
lished in accordance with these regula­
tions, including those not directly oper­
ated by the General Services Adminis­
tration.
S ec. 8. Discontinuance or curtailment  
of service, (a) If, during any reasonable 
period, not exceeding two successive fis­
cal years, no actual savings are realized 
from the operation of any pool or system 
established hereunder, the Administra­
tor shall discontinue the pool or system 
concerned.
(b) The Administrator may discon­
tinue or curtail a motor-vehicle pool or 
system when he determines that it is 
not the most economical method of ren­
dering required motor-vehicle service; 
but he shall give at least sixty days no­
tice of such intention to executive agen­
cies affected and to the Director before 
taking such action.
(c) Executive agencies affected by a 
pool or system for which the Adminis­
trator is responsible (including inter­
agency pools or systems operated by an­
other executive agency designated by the 
Administrator) may bring problems of 
service and cost to the attention of the. 
Administrator, who shall assure that 
such problems receive proper attention.
(d) Executive agencies  receiving 
motor-vehicle services from an inter­
agency motor-vehicle pool or system 
under these regulations may request dis­
continuance or curtailment of their par­
ticipation in such pool or system after 
at least one year of participation or in 
the event that the need for the services 
from the pool or system ceases. Such 
requests shall be submitted to the Ad­
ministrator with pertinent factual justi­
fication.
(e) If the Administrator does not 
agree with such request and is unable to 
make arrangements which are mutually 
acceptable to him and to the head of the 
executive agency concerned, the agency’ s 
request for discontinuance or modifica­
tion and the Administrator’ s reasons for 
not agreeing with the request shall be 
forwarded to the Director who shall be 
responsible for making a final and bind­
ing decision.
(f) When a pool or system is discon­
tinued or curtailed, such transfers of 
vehicles and related equipment and sup­
plies, personnel, records, facilities, and 
funds as may be appropriate will be 
made, subject to the approval of the 
Director.
S ec. 9. Motor vehicles exempted from  
inclusion in interagency motor-vehicle  
pools. The following-described classes 
of motor vehicles shall be exempt from 
inclusion in\ interagency motor-vehicle 
pools or systems:
(1) Motor vehicles designed or used 
for military field training, combat, or 
tactical purposes, or used principally 
within the confines of a regularly estab­
lished military post, camp, or depot.
(2) Any motor vehicle regularly used 
by an agency in the performance of in­
vestigative, law enforcement, or intelli­
gence duties if the head of such agency 
determines that exclusive control of such 
vehicle is essential to the effective per­
formance of such duties: Provided, that 
vehicles regularly used for common ad­
ministrative purposes not directly con­
nected with the performance of law 
enforcement, investigative, or intelli­
gence duties shall not because of such 
use be exempted from such inclusion.
(3) Any motor vehicle the conspicu­
ous identification of which as a Govern­
ment vehicle would interfere with the 
purpose for which it is acquired and 
used.
(4) Unless inclusion is mutually agreed 
upon by the Administrator and the head 
of the agency concerned:
(i) Motor vehicles for the use of the 
heads of the executive agencies, ambas­
sadors, ministers, chargé d’ affaires, and 
other principal diplomatic and consular 
officials.
(ii) Motor vehicles regularly and prin­
cipally used for the transportation of 
diplomats and representatives of foreign 
countries or by officers of the Depart­
ment of State for the conduct of official 
business with representatives of foreign 
countries.
(iii) Motor vehicles regularly used for 
the distribution and transportation of 
mails.
(5) Motor vehicles which, because of 
their design or the special purposes for 
which they are used, or for other reasons, 
cannot advantageously be incorporated 
in an interagency motor-vehicle pool or 
system if the exemption thereof has been 
mutually agreed upon by the Adminis­
trator and the head of the executive 
agency concerned.
(6) Motor vehicles exempted by an 
agency which ljas authority to make such 
an exemption under the provisions of the 
Act.
S ec. 10. Optional use arrangements.  
Nothing in these regulations shall be 
construed as precluding the establish­
ment or operation of interagency motor- 
vehicle pools or systems on the basis of 
optional use by executive or other Fed­
eral agencies.
S ec. 11. Supplementary regulations.  
The Administrator shall, after consulta­
tion with the executive agencies con­
cerned and with due regard to their 
program activities, issue such supple­
mentary regulations of general applica­
bility to the executive agencies concerned 
as are necessary for the effective and eco­
nomical operation of pools or systems 
under the Act.

By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Federal Property and Adminis­
trative Services Act of 1949, as amended 
(hereinafter referred to as the Act), 
particularly by sections 107, 205 (a) and 
211 (c) thereof, 63 Stat. 382, 389, 64 Stat.

States, I hereby prescribe the following 
regulations: t
S ection  1. Purpose and general policy.
(a) The purpose of these regulations is 
to establish policies and procedures un­
der which interagency motor-vehicle 
pools or systems may be established, op­
erated, curtailed, or discontinued.
(b) The Administrator of General 
Services (hereinafter referred to as the 
Administrator) shall establish and pro­
vide for the operation of interagency 
motor-vehicle pools and systems for the 
purpose of providing more efficient or 
economical transportation of Govern­
ment personnel and property within 
specific areas by motor vehicles or local 
transit systems. Pools or systems based 
in whole or in part upon use of privately- 
owned vehicles and facilities shall be 
preferred to Government ownership of 
vehicles and facilities to the extent that 
it is feasible to provide required motor- 
vehicle services of satisfactory quality 
and cost from commercial or other pri­
vate sources.
Sec. 2. Conduct of studies to deter­
mine advisability  o f establishing  
motor-vehicle pools or systems, (a) The 
Administrator shall select areas in which 
studies are to be conducted to determine 
the advisability of establishing motor- 
vehicle pools or systems. Before initiat­
ing any such study, he shall give at least 
thirty days notice to the head of each 
executive agency (as defined in section 
3 (a) of the Act). The notice shall in­
clude a statement of the approximate 
geographic area to be studied and the 
date on which the study will begin.
(b) The head of each executive agency 
receiving notice that such a study is to
be made shall provide information which 
is required or pertinent. He shall also 
designate one or more officials in the 
field with whom members of a staff as­
signed by the General Services Admin­
istration may consult. Such designated 
officials shall provide such assigned staff 
with needed information and assistance, 
including reasonable opportunities to 
observe motor-vehicle operations and 
facilities and to examine pertinent cost 
and other records.
Sec.  3. Determination to establish an  
interagency motor-vehicle pool or sys­
tem. (a) If the Administrator deter­
mines, with due regard to the program 
activities of the agencies concerned, and 
on the basis of a study made in accord­
ance with section 2 hereof, that an inter­
agency motor-vehicle pool or system 
should be established, he shall be respon­
sible for preparing a formal determina­
tion to that effect. Such determination 
shall include:(1) A description of the proposed op­
eration, including a statement of the 
types of service and of the geographic 
area, and the agencies or parts of agen­
cies to be served.(2) The name of the executive agency 
designated to be responsible for operat­
ing the pool or system, and the reasons 
for such designation.
(3) A statement indicating the motor 
vehicles and related equipment and sup­
plies to be transferred and the amount 
of reimbursement, if any, to be made 
therefor.
(b) Each determination shall be ac­
companied by an analytical justification 
which shall include a comparison of 
estimated costs of the present and pro­
posed methods of operation and a show­
ing of the estimated savings to be real­
ized through the establishment of the 
proposed pool or system. The justifica­
tion shall also describe the alternatives 
considered in making the determination, 
and shall include a statement concern­
ing the availability of privately-owned 
facilities and equipment, and the feasi­
bility and estimated cost (immediate and 
long-term) of using such facilities and 
equipment.

copy of each determination to each exec­
utive agency affected and to the Director

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Operative. Section 11 directs the Administrator, after consultation with the Director and the agencies concerned, to issue supplementary regulations for the effective and economical operation of pools or systems under the Act. The held text of 41 CFR part 101-39 cites the order; the claim does not decide whether that part is the supplementary regulations this section contemplates. It has no own-terms end, and no held instrument ends or amends it.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
S ec. 11. Supplementary regulations.  
The Administrator shall, after consulta­
tion with the executive agencies con­
cerned and with due regard to their 
program activities, issue such supple­
mentary regulations of general applica­
bility to the executive agencies concerned 
as are necessary for the effective and eco­
nomical operation of pools or systems 
under the Act.

By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Federal Property and Adminis­
trative Services Act of 1949, as amended 
(hereinafter referred to as the Act),

States, I hereby prescribe the following 
regulations: t
S ection  1. Purpose and general policy.
(a) The purpose of these regulations is 
to establish policies and procedures un­
der which interagency motor-vehicle 
pools or systems may be established, op­
erated, curtailed, or discontinued.
(b) The Administrator of General 
Services (hereinafter referred to as the 
Administrator) shall establish and pro­
vide for the operation of interagency 
motor-vehicle pools and systems for the 
purpose of providing more efficient or 
economical transportation of Govern­
ment personnel and property within 
specific areas by motor vehicles or local 
transit systems. Pools or systems based 
in whole or in part upon use of privately- 
owned vehicles and facilities shall be 
preferred to Government ownership of 
vehicles and facilities to the extent that 
it is feasible to provide required motor- 
vehicle services of satisfactory quality 
and cost from commercial or other pri­
vate sources.
Sec. 2. Conduct of studies to deter­
mine advisability  o f establishing  
motor-vehicle pools or systems, (a) The 
Administrator shall select areas in which 
studies are to be conducted to determine 
the advisability of establishing motor- 
vehicle pools or systems. Before initiat­
ing any such study, he shall give at least 
thirty days notice to the head of each 
executive agency (as defined in section 
3 (a) of the Act). The notice shall in­
clude a statement of the approximate 
geographic area to be studied and the 
date on which the study will begin.
(b) The head of each executive agency 
receiving notice that such a study is to
be made shall provide information which 
is required or pertinent. He shall also 
designate one or more officials in the 
field with whom members of a staff as­
signed by the General Services Admin­
istration may consult. Such designated 
officials shall provide such assigned staff 
with needed information and assistance, 
including reasonable opportunities to 
observe motor-vehicle operations and 
facilities and to examine pertinent cost 
and other records.
Sec.  3. Determination to establish an  
interagency motor-vehicle pool or sys­
tem. (a) If the Administrator deter­
mines, with due regard to the program 
activities of the agencies concerned, and 
on the basis of a study made in accord­
ance with section 2 hereof, that an inter­
agency motor-vehicle pool or system 
should be established, he shall be respon­
sible for preparing a formal determina­
tion to that effect. Such determination 
shall include:(1) A description of the proposed op­
eration, including a statement of the 
types of service and of the geographic 
area, and the agencies or parts of agen­
cies to be served.(2) The name of the executive agency 
designated to be responsible for operat­
ing the pool or system, and the reasons 
for such designation.
(3) A statement indicating the motor 
vehicles and related equipment and sup­
plies to be transferred and the amount 
of reimbursement, if any, to be made 
therefor.
(b) Each determination shall be ac­
companied by an analytical justification 
which shall include a comparison of 
estimated costs of the present and pro­
posed methods of operation and a show­
ing of the estimated savings to be real­
ized through the establishment of the 
proposed pool or system. The justifica­
tion shall also describe the alternatives 
considered in making the determination, 
and shall include a statement concern­
ing the availability of privately-owned 
facilities and equipment, and the feasi­
bility and estimated cost (immediate and 
long-term) of using such facilities and 
equipment.
(c) The Administrator shall send a 
copy of each determination to each exec­
utive agency affected and to the Director

S ec. 4. Transfers of records, facilities, 
personnel, and appropriations.  When­
ever the Administrator prepares a de­
termination as set forth in section 3  of 
these regulations, he shall also prepare 
and present to the Director a schedule of 
the proposed transfer of such records, 
facilities, personnel, and appropriations 
as relate primarily to the functions 
which are to be transferred to the inter­
agency motor-vehicle pool or system. A 
copy of such schedule shall be sent by 
the Administrator to each executive 
agency affected. The Director shall de­
termine the records, facilities, personnel, 
and appropriations to be transferred.
S ec. 5. Taking effect of determina­
tions. Unless a greater time is allowed 
therein, any determination made by the 
Administrator shall become binding on 
all affected executive agencies forty-five

days after the issuance thereof except 
with respect to any agency which ap­
peals, or requests an exemption, from 
any such determination in accordance 
with section 6 of these regulations.
Sec. 6. Review of determinations not  
agreed to by agencies affected, (a) Any 
executive agency may appeal or request 
exemption from any or all proposals af­
fecting it which are contained in a de­
termination. Appeals shall be submitted 
in writing to the Director with a copy to 
the Administrator within forty-five days 
from the date of the determination. 
Such appeals shall be accompanied by 
factual and objective supporting data 
and justification.
(b) The Director shall review any de­
termination from which an executive 
agency has appealed and shall make a 
final decision on such appeal. The Di­
rector shall make such decisions, within 
seventy-five days after he receives the 
appeal or as soon thereafter as prac­
ticable, on the basis of information con­
tained in the Administrator’ s determi­
nation, the executive agencies’  appeals 
therefrom, and any supplementary data 
submitted by the Administrator and the 
contesting agencies. The Director shall 
send copies of decisions to the Adminis­
trator and to the heads of other execu­
tive agencies concerned.
(c) The Director’ s decision upon each 
such appeal, if it holds that the deter­
mination shall apply in whole or in part 
to the appealing agency, shall state the 
extent to which the determination ap­
plies and the effective date of its appli­
cation. To the extent that the Director’ s 
decision on an appeal does not uphold 
the Administrator’ s determination, such 
determination shall be of no force and 
effect.
S ec. 7. Compliance with determina­
tions and decisions on appeals, (a) When 
a determination or a decision on an ap­
peal made in accordance with these 
regulations has become effective, each 
executive agency affected shall comply 
therewith.(b) The Director shall take such ac­
tions as he deems appropriate to assist 
in securing compliance with determina­
tions which have become effective. In 
the exercise of his authority to establish 
reserves in apportioning appropriations 
and funds, the Director shall take ac­
count of such savings as accrue from 
the establishment of interagency motor- 
vehicle pools and systems.
(c) The executive agency which op­
erates any pool or system established 
hereunder shall maintain accurate rec­
ords of the cost of establishment, main­
tenance, and operation of any inter­
agency motor-vehicle pool or system 
established pursuant to these regula­
tions.
(d) The Administrator shall be re­
sponsible for maintaining adequate re­
views and controls of the economy and
efficiency of all pools or systems estab­
lished in accordance with these regula­
tions, including those not directly oper­
ated by the General Services Adminis­
tration.
S ec. 8. Discontinuance or curtailment  
of service, (a) If, during any reasonable 
period, not exceeding two successive fis­
cal years, no actual savings are realized 
from the operation of any pool or system 
established hereunder, the Administra­
tor shall discontinue the pool or system 
concerned.
(b) The Administrator may discon­
tinue or curtail a motor-vehicle pool or 
system when he determines that it is 
not the most economical method of ren­
dering required motor-vehicle service; 
but he shall give at least sixty days no­
tice of such intention to executive agen­
cies affected and to the Director before 
taking such action.
(c) Executive agencies affected by a 
pool or system for which the Adminis­
trator is responsible (including inter­
agency pools or systems operated by an­
other executive agency designated by the 
Administrator) may bring problems of 
service and cost to the attention of the. 
Administrator, who shall assure that 
such problems receive proper attention.
(d) Executive agencies  receiving 
motor-vehicle services from an inter­
agency motor-vehicle pool or system 
under these regulations may request dis­
continuance or curtailment of their par­
ticipation in such pool or system after 
at least one year of participation or in 
the event that the need for the services 
from the pool or system ceases. Such 
requests shall be submitted to the Ad­
ministrator with pertinent factual justi­
fication.
(e) If the Administrator does not 
agree with such request and is unable to 
make arrangements which are mutually 
acceptable to him and to the head of the 
executive agency concerned, the agency’ s 
request for discontinuance or modifica­
tion and the Administrator’ s reasons for 
not agreeing with the request shall be 
forwarded to the Director who shall be 
responsible for making a final and bind­
ing decision.
(f) When a pool or system is discon­
tinued or curtailed, such transfers of 
vehicles and related equipment and sup­
plies, personnel, records, facilities, and 
funds as may be appropriate will be 
made, subject to the approval of the 
Director.
S ec. 9. Motor vehicles exempted from  
inclusion in interagency motor-vehicle  
pools. The following-described classes 
of motor vehicles shall be exempt from 
inclusion in\ interagency motor-vehicle 
pools or systems:
(1) Motor vehicles designed or used 
for military field training, combat, or 
tactical purposes, or used principally 
within the confines of a regularly estab­
lished military post, camp, or depot.
(2) Any motor vehicle regularly used 
by an agency in the performance of in­
vestigative, law enforcement, or intelli­
gence duties if the head of such agency 
determines that exclusive control of such 
vehicle is essential to the effective per­
formance of such duties: Provided, that 
vehicles regularly used for common ad­
ministrative purposes not directly con­
nected with the performance of law 
enforcement, investigative, or intelli­
gence duties shall not because of such 
use be exempted from such inclusion.
(3) Any motor vehicle the conspicu­
ous identification of which as a Govern­
ment vehicle would interfere with the 
purpose for which it is acquired and 
used.
(4) Unless inclusion is mutually agreed 
upon by the Administrator and the head 
of the agency concerned:
(i) Motor vehicles for the use of the 
heads of the executive agencies, ambas­
sadors, ministers, chargé d’ affaires, and 
other principal diplomatic and consular 
officials.
(ii) Motor vehicles regularly and prin­
cipally used for the transportation of 
diplomats and representatives of foreign 
countries or by officers of the Depart­
ment of State for the conduct of official 
business with representatives of foreign 
countries.
(iii) Motor vehicles regularly used for 
the distribution and transportation of 
mails.
(5) Motor vehicles which, because of 
their design or the special purposes for 
which they are used, or for other reasons, 
cannot advantageously be incorporated 
in an interagency motor-vehicle pool or 
system if the exemption thereof has been 
mutually agreed upon by the Adminis­
trator and the head of the executive 
agency concerned.
(6) Motor vehicles exempted by an 
agency which ljas authority to make such 
an exemption under the provisions of the 
Act.
S ec. 10. Optional use arrangements.  
Nothing in these regulations shall be 
construed as precluding the establish­
ment or operation of interagency motor- 
vehicle pools or systems on the basis of 
optional use by executive or other Fed­
eral agencies.
S ec. 11. Supplementary regulations.  
The Administrator shall, after consulta­
tion with the executive agencies con­
cerned and with due regard to their 
program activities, issue such supple­
mentary regulations of general applica­
bility to the executive agencies concerned 
as are necessary for the effective and eco­
nomical operation of pools or systems 
under the Act.

research_rationale:
EO 10579 (19 FR 7925, signed 1954-11-30) prescribes regulations under which the Administrator of General Services establishes, operates, curtails and discontinues interagency motor-vehicle pools and systems. I read the held Federal Register original in full (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10579.txt): the number, title, date, signature and filing line (F.R. Doc. 54-9551) agree. The dossier listed 35 fragments, some inside printed contents-page text, so I replaced them with 12 spans of the order's own text (Section 3 in two parts around the page break). The order has eleven sections with no expiry date; its day counts (thirty-day notice, forty-five-day appeals, seventy-five-day decisions) and the discontinuance conditions are procedures for each study, determination, appeal or pool, not ends of the sections. The dossier's machine own-terms leads on Sections 5, 8(f) and 9 are of that kind. No later instrument is held that amends, revokes or supersedes the order: the OFR disposition table lists none for EO 10579, the later-events catalog search found 0 hits, and the held-text number search lists only the 1989 OFR Codification and the 41 CFR part 101-39 text, which cite it as in use. The dossier lists EO 10578 as a possible acting order, but the held ProQuest replica of EO 10578 shows only the adjacent page of the issue (EO 10578 concerns railroad labor disputes and the replica also prints the heading of EO 10579); it contains no provision amending EO 10579. EO 12608 (1987) section 2 substitutes the Office of Management and Budget for the Bureau of the Budget in orders listed there and in any other order that relates to functions delegated to that Office; it does not name EO 10579, the OFR table does not list it for EO 10579, and the packet holds it as no evidence record, so it is recorded here only as a possible wording change to the references to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget and is not claimed as an ending. Authority: the order cites the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949 (sections 107, 205(a) and 211(c)) and section 202 of the Budget and Accounting Procedures Act of 1950; those provisions have since been restated in other titles of the U.S. Code and no restated text is held here, so the claim rests on the held current regulations that still cite the order as their governing instrument rather than on the successor statutes' text. Current predicate: original-plus-bounded-search route after reading the coverage of the three searches.

Sec. 6. Review of determinations not  
agreed to by agencies affected, (a) Any 
executive agency may appeal or request 
exemption from any or all proposals af­
fecting it which are contained in a de­
termination. Appeals shall be submitted 
in writing to the Director with a copy to 
the Administrator within forty-five days 
from the date of the determination. 
Such appeals shall be accompanied by 
factual and objective supporting data 
and justification.
(b) The Director shall review any de­
termination from which an executive 
agency has appealed and shall make a 
final decision on such appeal. The Di­
rector shall make such decisions, within 
seventy-five days after he receives the 
appeal or as soon thereafter as prac­
ticable, on the basis of information con­
tained in the Administrator’ s determi­
nation, the executive agencies’  appeals

trator and to the heads of other execu­

(c) The Director’ s decision upon each 
such appeal, if it holds that the deter­
mination shall apply in whole or in part 
to the appealing agency, shall state the

plies and the effective date of its appli­
cation. To the extent that the Director’ s 
decision on an appeal does not uphold 
the Administrator’ s determination, such 
determination shall be of no force and 
effect.
S ec. 7. Compliance with determina­
tions and decisions on appeals, (a) When 
a determination or a decision on an ap­
peal made in accordance with these 
regulations has become effective, each 
executive agency affected shall comply 
therewith.(b) The Director shall take such ac­
tions as he deems appropriate to assist 
in securing compliance with determina­
tions which have become effective. In 
the exercise of his authority to establish 
reserves in apportioning appropriations 
and funds, the Director shall take ac­
count of such savings as accrue from 
the establishment of interagency motor- 
vehicle pools and systems.

erates any pool or system established

ords of the cost of establishment, main­
tenance, and operation of any inter­
agency motor-vehicle pool or system

tions.

sponsible for maintaining adequate re­
views and controls of the economy and
efficiency of all pools or systems estab­
lished in accordance with these regula­
tions, including those not directly oper­
ated by the General Services Adminis­
tration.
S ec. 8. Discontinuance or curtailment  
of service, (a) If, during any reasonable 
period, not exceeding two successive fis­
cal years, no actual savings are realized 
from the operation of any pool or system 
established hereunder, the Administra­
tor shall discontinue the pool or system 
concerned.
(b) The Administrator may discon­
tinue or curtail a motor-vehicle pool or 
system when he determines that it is

dering required motor-vehicle service; 
but he shall give at least sixty days no­
tice of such intention to executive agen­
cies affected and to the Director before 
taking such action.
(c) Executive agencies affected by a

trator is responsible (including inter­
agency pools or systems operated by an­
other executive agency designated by the 
Administrator) may bring problems of 
service and cost to the attention of the. 
Administrator, who shall assure that 
such problems receive proper attention.
(d) Executive agencies  receiving 
motor-vehicle services from an inter­
agency motor-vehicle pool or system 
under these regulations may request dis­
continuance or curtailment of their par­
ticipation in such pool or system after 
at least one year of participation or in 
the event that the need for the services 
from the pool or system ceases. Such 
requests shall be submitted to the Ad­
ministrator with pertinent factual justi­
fication.

agree with such request and is unable to

acceptable to him and to the head of the 
executive agency concerned, the agency’ s 
request for discontinuance or modifica­
tion and the Administrator’ s reasons for 
not agreeing with the request shall be 
forwarded to the Director who shall be 
responsible for making a final and bind­
ing decision.

tinued or curtailed, such transfers of 
vehicles and related equipment and sup­
plies, personnel, records, facilities, and 
funds as may be appropriate will be 
made, subject to the approval of the 
Director.
S ec. 9. Motor vehicles exempted from  
inclusion in interagency motor-vehicle  
pools. The following-described classes 
of motor vehicles shall be exempt from 
inclusion in\ interagency motor-vehicle 
pools or systems:
(1) Motor vehicles designed or used 
for military field training, combat, or 
tactical purposes, or used principally 
within the confines of a regularly estab­
lished military post, camp, or depot.
(2) Any motor vehicle regularly used 
by an agency in the performance of in­
vestigative, law enforcement, or intelli­
gence duties if the head of such agency 
determines that exclusive control of such 
vehicle is essential to the effective per­
formance of such duties: Provided, that 
vehicles regularly used for common ad­
ministrative purposes not directly con­
nected with the performance of law 
enforcement, investigative, or intelli­
gence duties shall not because of such 
use be exempted from such inclusion.
(3) Any motor vehicle the conspicu­
ous identification of which as a Govern­
ment vehicle would interfere with the 
purpose for which it is acquired and 
used.
(4) Unless inclusion is mutually agreed 
upon by the Administrator and the head 
of the agency concerned:
(i) Motor vehicles for the use of the 
heads of the executive agencies, ambas­
sadors, ministers, chargé d’ affaires, and 
other principal diplomatic and consular 
officials.
(ii) Motor vehicles regularly and prin­
cipally used for the transportation of 
diplomats and representatives of foreign 
countries or by officers of the Depart­
ment of State for the conduct of official 
business with representatives of foreign 
countries.
(iii) Motor vehicles regularly used for 
the distribution and transportation of 
mails.
(5) Motor vehicles which, because of 
their design or the special purposes for 
which they are used, or for other reasons, 
cannot advantageously be incorporated 
in an interagency motor-vehicle pool or 
system if the exemption thereof has been 
mutually agreed upon by the Adminis­
trator and the head of the executive 
agency concerned.
(6) Motor vehicles exempted by an 
agency which ljas authority to make such 
an exemption under the provisions of the 
Act.
S ec. 10. Optional use arrangements.  
Nothing in these regulations shall be 
construed as precluding the establish­
ment or operation of interagency motor- 
vehicle pools or systems on the basis of 
optional use by executive or other Fed­
eral agencies.
S ec. 11. Supplementary regulations.  
The Administrator shall, after consulta­
tion with the executive agencies con­
cerned and with due regard to their 
program activities, issue such supple­
mentary regulations of general applica­
bility to the executive agencies concerned 
as are necessary for the effective and eco­
nomical operation of pools or systems 
under the Act.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Rule VIII lets the Commission, now the Office of Personnel Management, authorize recruitment and appointment of persons to overseas positions: overseas limited appointments for United States citizens recruited overseas (section 8.2), appointment of non-citizens (section 8.3), and exclusion of positions in Hawaii, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Alaska and the Isthmus of Panama (section 8.4). EO 12107 section 2-101 substituted Office of Personnel Management for Civil Service Commission effective 1979-01-01; that is a wording amendment, so the clause continues in amended form. No held instrument revokes or supersedes Rule VIII or its parent EO 10577. The held 5 CFR part 301 text (outside this claim's cited sources) cites the order as authority for current overseas-employment regulations.

research_rationale:
EO 10641 (20 FR 8137, signed 1955-10-26) amends the Civil Service Rules prescribed by EO 10577 by adding Rule VIII, Appointments to Overseas Positions (sections 8.1 to 8.4). I read the held Federal Register original in full (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10641.txt, characters 759-3469 for the order's operative paragraph): the number, title, date, signature line and filing line (F.R. Doc. 55-8799) agree, and the page text after it belongs to EO 10642, which is a different order. The dossier lists one clause, the whole amendment instruction containing Rule VIII, and I kept that inventory: Rule VIII is added as a single instrument and the claim does not separate its four sections. The order has no expiry date. The machine own-terms leads in the dossier are conditions on the Commission's authority in section 8.2 (a shortage-of-registers finding that the Commission makes) and a retirement-act exclusion in the same section; they condition particular appointments and do not end the rule. Later events: EO 12107 (44 FR 1055, signed 1978-12-28, effective 1979-01-01) section 2-101 amends the order by substituting Office of Personnel Management for Civil Service Commission and related titles in the orders listed there, which include EO 10641; its section 2-103 amends Rules II, IV and V of EO 10577 but not Rule VIII; its general effective date is 1979-01-01. The OFR disposition table lists only EO 12107 as amending EO 10641. Two later orders held in the repository refer to Rule VIII without amending it: EO 12362 (1982) section 4 and EO 12721 (1990) section 3 each say that, to the extent of any conflict, the order controls over Civil Service Rule 8.2 (5 CFR 8.2). A precedence-in-conflict rule treats Rule 8.2 as existing and does not revoke or supersede it. Those texts are not evidence records in this packet, so they cannot be cited as later events here; I note them for the reviewer. Current predicate: original-plus-bounded-search route, after reading the coverage of current-law:usc (release point current through 2026-10-09; later laws to 2026-10-14 not reflected), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog. The held eCFR text of 5 CFR part 301 (Overseas Employment, jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/cfr-t5-part301.txt, GovInfo eCFR bulk amended through 2026) cites E.O. 10577 as amended by E.O. 10641 in its authority line, and its subpart B regulates overseas limited appointments, the subject of section 8.2; that is context from the ecfr search and not a cited source. EO 10577, which prescribes the rules Rule VIII was added to, is not revoked in the OFR table (it lists amendments only), and held EO 13467 (2008) and EO 13764 (2017) each state that nothing in them supersedes EO 10577 as amended.

The OFR disposition table lists only EO 12107 as amending it, and the later-events catalog search reports 2 hits for it, which are the OFR disposition note for the EO 12107 amendment and a see-reference to EO 10577. The held-text number search finds EO 10577 (the parent), a 1995 and a 2025 Federal Register document and 5 CFR text that cite it as authority; none revokes it. EO 12362 and EO 12721 mention Rule 8.2 only in a precedence-in-conflict section and neither revokes or supersedes Rule VIII.","independent_command_check":"Rule VIII sections 8.1 to 8.4 are one grant of authority with its conditions and one exclusion; none is a separate dated or conditional command that could have ended on its own, and no held source shows any of them ended.","savings_check":"No savings clause exists in the order and no later order is held that saved or transferred anything. The claim records the savings state as none after bounded search.","scope_check":"The target of the instrument is Rule VIII only. EO 12107 section 2-103 changes Rules II, IV and V of EO 10577 and does not touch Rule VIII, and the title substitution in section 2-101 is a wording amendment, not an ending. A revocation of part of EO 10577 would have to be checked against Rule VIII; the OFR table shows no revocation of any part of EO 10577."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order has no savings or transition clause and the claim asserts that Rule VIII continues. The only held later event is a change of agency names. The retirement-act exclusion in section 8.2 is part of the same clause and is not separately claimed as ended or continuing beyond what the clause-level basis supports.
